blocks.prompt: 3 (i) Find the inverse of the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = x^2 - 3,\ x \le 0\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic is not one-one on all real numbers, but on the given half of the parabola (one side of the vertex) it is, so an inverse exists.
We must find \(f^{-1}(x)\) and the domain and range of \(f^{-1}\).
Plan: write \(f\) in vertex form to get its range; swap \(x\) and \(y\); solve for \(y\); keep the sign of the root that matches the given domain; then Domain \(f^{-1}\) = Range \(f\) and Range \(f^{-1}\) = Domain \(f\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^2 - 3\) with domain \(x \le 0\) (the left half of the parabola).
To find: \(f^{-1}(x)\), Domain \(f^{-1}\) and Range \(f^{-1}\).
Method: swap \(x\) and \(y\), solve for \(y\), and choose the sign using \(y \le 0\).

Domain and range of \(f\)
\[\text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ 0]\]
\[x \le 0 \Rightarrow x^2 \ge 0 \Rightarrow x^2 - 3 \ge -3\]
\[\text{Range } f = [-3,\ \infty)\]
Why: the vertex is \((0, -3)\) and \(x = 0\) is allowed, so \(-3\) is reached; as \(x\) goes to \(-\infty\), \(x^2\) grows without limit.

Swap \(x\) and \(y\)
\[y = x^2 - 3 \;\longrightarrow\; x = y^2 - 3\]
Why: the inverse undoes \(f\): if \(f\) sends \(a\) to \(b\), then \(f^{-1}\) sends \(b\) back to \(a\). Swapping \(x\) and \(y\) expresses exactly this.

Solve for \(y\)
\[y^2 = x + 3\]
\[y = \pm\sqrt{x + 3}\]
Why: add 3 to both sides, then take the square root; a square root gives two signs.

Choose the sign
\[y \le 0 \Rightarrow y = -\sqrt{x + 3}\]
\[f^{-1}(x) = -\sqrt{x + 3}\]
Why: the outputs of \(f^{-1}\) must be the inputs of \(f\), which are \(\le 0\). \(+\sqrt{x + 3}\) is never negative, so it would give the wrong half.

Domain and range of \(f^{-1}\)
\[\text{Domain } f^{-1} = \text{Range } f = [-3,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f^{-1} = \text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ 0]\]
Why: the inputs of \(f^{-1}\) are the outputs of \(f\), and its outputs are the inputs of \(f\). (Also: \(\sqrt{x + 3}\) needs \(x \ge -3\).)

Check
\[f(-2) = 4 - 3 = 1\]
\[f^{-1}(1) = -\sqrt{4} = -2 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(f^{-1}\) brings the output 1 back to the input \(-2\).

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) Find the inverse of the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 4,\ x < -3\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic is not one-one on all real numbers, but on the given half of the parabola (one side of the vertex) it is, so an inverse exists.
We must find \(f^{-1}(x)\) and the domain and range of \(f^{-1}\).
Plan: write \(f\) in vertex form to get its range; swap \(x\) and \(y\); solve for \(y\); keep the sign of the root that matches the given domain; then Domain \(f^{-1}\) = Range \(f\) and Range \(f^{-1}\) = Domain \(f\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 4\) with domain \(x < -3\).
To find: \(f^{-1}(x)\), Domain \(f^{-1}\) and Range \(f^{-1}\).
Method: vertex form, swap, solve, choose the sign using \(y < -3\).

Vertex form
\[f(x) = x^2 + 6x + 9 - 9 + 4\]
\[f(x) = (x + 3)^2 - 5\]
Why: half of 6 is 3 and \(3^2 = 9\); add and subtract 9. The vertex is \((-3, -5)\).

Domain and range of \(f\)
\[x < -3 \Rightarrow (x + 3)^2 > 0\]
\[\text{Range } f = (-5,\ \infty)\]
Why: \(x = -3\) is not allowed (strict \(<\)), so \((x + 3)^2\) is never 0 and \(f(x)\) never equals \(-5\); it takes every value above \(-5\).

Swap and solve
\[x = (y + 3)^2 - 5\]
\[(y + 3)^2 = x + 5\]
\[y + 3 = \pm\sqrt{x + 5}\]
Why: the inverse undoes \(f\): if \(f\) sends \(a\) to \(b\), then \(f^{-1}\) sends \(b\) back to \(a\). Swapping \(x\) and \(y\) expresses exactly this. Then isolate the square and take the root (two signs).

Choose the sign
\[y < -3 \Rightarrow y + 3 < 0\]
\[y = -3 - \sqrt{x + 5}\]
\[f^{-1}(x) = -3 - \sqrt{x + 5}\]
Why: \(y + 3\) must be negative, so we keep \(-\sqrt{x + 5}\). (The book's quadratic-formula working gives the same two candidates \(y = -3 \pm \sqrt{x + 5}\).)

Domain and range of \(f^{-1}\)
\[\text{Domain } f^{-1} = \text{Range } f = (-5,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f^{-1} = \text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ -3)\]
Why: the inputs of \(f^{-1}\) are the outputs of \(f\), and its outputs are the inputs of \(f\). Indeed \(-3 - \sqrt{x + 5}\) is always less than \(-3\).

Check
\[f(-5) = 25 - 30 + 4 = -1\]
\[f^{-1}(-1) = -3 - \sqrt{4} = -5 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(f^{-1}\) sends the output \(-1\) back to the input \(-5\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (book page 296) prints Range \(f^{-1} = (-3,\ \infty)\) for Q3 (ii). The range of \(f^{-1}\) is the domain of \(f\), which is \(x < -3\); so the correct range is \((-\infty,\ -3)\). The printed \(f^{-1}(x)\) and domain are right.

blocks.prompt: 3 (iii) Find the inverse of the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 8x + 11,\ x \ge 2\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic is not one-one on all real numbers, but on the given half of the parabola (one side of the vertex) it is, so an inverse exists.
We must find \(f^{-1}(x)\) and the domain and range of \(f^{-1}\).
Plan: write \(f\) in vertex form to get its range; swap \(x\) and \(y\); solve for \(y\); keep the sign of the root that matches the given domain; then Domain \(f^{-1}\) = Range \(f\) and Range \(f^{-1}\) = Domain \(f\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 8x + 11\) with domain \(x \ge 2\).
To find: \(f^{-1}(x)\), Domain \(f^{-1}\) and Range \(f^{-1}\).
Method: vertex form, swap, solve, choose the sign using \(y \ge 2\).

Vertex form
\[f(x) = 2(x^2 - 4x) + 11\]
\[f(x) = 2(x^2 - 4x + 4 - 4) + 11\]
\[f(x) = 2(x - 2)^2 - 8 + 11\]
\[f(x) = 2(x - 2)^2 + 3\]
Why: take 2 common from the \(x\)-terms; half of \(-4\) is \(-2\), squared 4; the \(-4\) inside becomes \(-8\) outside.

Domain and range of \(f\)
\[x \ge 2 \Rightarrow 2(x - 2)^2 \ge 0\]
\[\text{Range } f = [3,\ \infty)\]
Why: the given domain starts exactly at the vertex \((2, 3)\) and includes it, so the least output 3 is reached.

Swap and solve
\[x = 2(y - 2)^2 + 3\]
\[(y - 2)^2 = \dfrac{x - 3}{2}\]
\[y - 2 = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{x - 3}{2}}\]
Why: the inverse undoes \(f\): if \(f\) sends \(a\) to \(b\), then \(f^{-1}\) sends \(b\) back to \(a\). Swapping \(x\) and \(y\) expresses exactly this.

Choose the sign and simplify
\[y \ge 2 \Rightarrow y = 2 + \sqrt{\dfrac{x - 3}{2}}\]
\[\sqrt{\dfrac{x - 3}{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2(x - 3)}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2(x - 3)}}{2}\]
\[f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4 + \sqrt{2(x - 3)}}{2}\]
Why: \(y - 2 \ge 0\), so the \(+\) root. Multiplying inside the root by \(\tfrac{2}{2}\) gives the form of the answer key.

Domain and range of \(f^{-1}\)
\[\text{Domain } f^{-1} = \text{Range } f = [3,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f^{-1} = \text{Domain } f = [2,\ \infty)\]
Why: the inputs of \(f^{-1}\) are the outputs of \(f\), and its outputs are the inputs of \(f\). Also \(\sqrt{2(x - 3)}\) is real only for \(x \ge 3\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (book page 296) prints, for Q3 (iii), the root as \(\sqrt{2\ -3 + x}\) without brackets and Domain \(f^{-1} = [-3,\ \infty)\). Correct: \(f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4 + \sqrt{2(x - 3)}}{2}\) and Domain \(f^{-1} = [3,\ \infty)\) (the range of \(f = 2(x - 2)^2 + 3\) on \(x \ge 2\)). The range \([2,\ \infty)\) is right.

blocks.prompt: 3 (iv) Find the inverse of the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 2x + 6,\ x \ge 5\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic is not one-one on all real numbers, but on the given half of the parabola (one side of the vertex) it is, so an inverse exists.
We must find \(f^{-1}(x)\) and the domain and range of \(f^{-1}\).
Plan: write \(f\) in vertex form to get its range; swap \(x\) and \(y\); solve for \(y\); keep the sign of the root that matches the given domain; then Domain \(f^{-1}\) = Range \(f\) and Range \(f^{-1}\) = Domain \(f\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 2x + 6\) with domain \(x \ge 5\).
To find: \(f^{-1}(x)\), Domain \(f^{-1}\) and Range \(f^{-1}\).
Method: vertex form, swap, solve, choose the sign using \(y \ge 5\).

Vertex form
\[f(x) = 3\left(x^2 - \tfrac{2}{3}x\right) + 6\]
\[f(x) = 3\left(x^2 - \tfrac{2}{3}x + \tfrac{1}{9} - \tfrac{1}{9}\right) + 6\]
\[f(x) = 3\left(x - \tfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 - \tfrac{1}{3} + 6\]
\[f(x) = 3\left(x - \tfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 + \tfrac{17}{3}\]
Why: half of \(\tfrac{2}{3}\) is \(\tfrac{1}{3}\), squared \(\tfrac{1}{9}\); \(3 \times (-\tfrac{1}{9}) = -\tfrac{1}{3}\) and \(6 - \tfrac{1}{3} = \tfrac{17}{3}\).

Domain and range of \(f\)
\[f(5) = 75 - 10 + 6 = 71\]
\[\text{Range } f = [71,\ \infty)\]
Why: the vertex \(x = \tfrac{1}{3}\) is not in the domain. For \(x \ge 5\) we are to the right of the vertex, where \(f\) increases, so the least output is \(f(5) = 71\), not \(\tfrac{17}{3}\).

Swap and solve
\[x = 3\left(y - \tfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 + \tfrac{17}{3}\]
\[\left(y - \tfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{3x - 17}{9}\]
\[y - \tfrac{1}{3} = \pm\dfrac{\sqrt{3x - 17}}{3}\]
Why: the inverse undoes \(f\): if \(f\) sends \(a\) to \(b\), then \(f^{-1}\) sends \(b\) back to \(a\). Swapping \(x\) and \(y\) expresses exactly this. Here \(\tfrac{x - 17/3}{3} = \tfrac{3x - 17}{9}\) and \(\sqrt{9} = 3\).

Choose the sign
\[y \ge 5 \Rightarrow y - \tfrac{1}{3} > 0\]
\[f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{3x - 17}}{3}\]
Why: the \(-\) sign would give \(y \le \tfrac{1}{3}\), far below 5, so we keep \(+\).

Domain and range of \(f^{-1}\)
\[\text{Domain } f^{-1} = \text{Range } f = [71,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f^{-1} = \text{Domain } f = [5,\ \infty)\]
Why: the inputs of \(f^{-1}\) are the outputs of \(f\), and its outputs are the inputs of \(f\). (The formula alone would accept \(x \ge \tfrac{17}{3}\), but only \(x \ge 71\) are outputs of the given \(f\).)

blocks.prompt: 3 (v) Find the inverse of the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = 2(x - 3)^2 + 1,\ x \ge 3\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic is not one-one on all real numbers, but on the given half of the parabola (one side of the vertex) it is, so an inverse exists.
We must find \(f^{-1}(x)\) and the domain and range of \(f^{-1}\).
Plan: write \(f\) in vertex form to get its range; swap \(x\) and \(y\); solve for \(y\); keep the sign of the root that matches the given domain; then Domain \(f^{-1}\) = Range \(f\) and Range \(f^{-1}\) = Domain \(f\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 2(x - 3)^2 + 1\) with domain \(x \ge 3\). It is already in vertex form, vertex \((3, 1)\).
To find: \(f^{-1}(x)\), Domain \(f^{-1}\) and Range \(f^{-1}\).
Method: swap, solve, choose the sign using \(y \ge 3\).

Domain and range of \(f\)
\[x \ge 3 \Rightarrow 2(x - 3)^2 \ge 0\]
\[\text{Range } f = [1,\ \infty)\]
Why: the domain starts at the vertex and includes it, so the least output is \(f(3) = 1\).

Swap and solve
\[x = 2(y - 3)^2 + 1\]
\[(y - 3)^2 = \dfrac{x - 1}{2}\]
\[y - 3 = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{x - 1}{2}}\]
Why: the inverse undoes \(f\): if \(f\) sends \(a\) to \(b\), then \(f^{-1}\) sends \(b\) back to \(a\). Swapping \(x\) and \(y\) expresses exactly this.

Choose the sign
\[y \ge 3 \Rightarrow y = 3 + \sqrt{\dfrac{x - 1}{2}}\]
Why: \(y - 3 \ge 0\), so the \(+\) root.

Domain and range of \(f^{-1}\)
\[\text{Domain } f^{-1} = \text{Range } f = [1,\ \infty)\]
\[\text{Range } f^{-1} = \text{Domain } f = [3,\ \infty)\]
Why: the inputs of \(f^{-1}\) are the outputs of \(f\), and its outputs are the inputs of \(f\).

blocks.prompt: 3 (vi) Find the inverse of the following quadratic function. Also find its domain and range: \(f(x) = -3(x + 4)^2 - 5,\ x < -4\).
blocks.explanation:
A quadratic is not one-one on all real numbers, but on the given half of the parabola (one side of the vertex) it is, so an inverse exists.
We must find \(f^{-1}(x)\) and the domain and range of \(f^{-1}\).
Plan: write \(f\) in vertex form to get its range; swap \(x\) and \(y\); solve for \(y\); keep the sign of the root that matches the given domain; then Domain \(f^{-1}\) = Range \(f\) and Range \(f^{-1}\) = Domain \(f\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = -3(x + 4)^2 - 5\) with domain \(x < -4\). Vertex form, vertex \((-4, -5)\), opening downward.
To find: \(f^{-1}(x)\), Domain \(f^{-1}\) and Range \(f^{-1}\).
Method: swap, solve, choose the sign using \(y < -4\).

Domain and range of \(f\)
\[x < -4 \Rightarrow (x + 4)^2 > 0\]
\[-3(x + 4)^2 < 0 \Rightarrow f(x) < -5\]
\[\text{Range } f = (-\infty,\ -5)\]
Why: \(x = -4\) is excluded (strict \(<\)), so the vertex value \(-5\) is never reached; the outputs fall without limit.

Swap and solve
\[x = -3(y + 4)^2 - 5\]
\[(y + 4)^2 = \dfrac{-(x + 5)}{3}\]
\[y + 4 = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{-(x + 5)}{3}}\]
Why: the inverse undoes \(f\): if \(f\) sends \(a\) to \(b\), then \(f^{-1}\) sends \(b\) back to \(a\). Swapping \(x\) and \(y\) expresses exactly this. Note \(-(x + 5) > 0\) because \(x < -5\).

Choose the sign
\[y < -4 \Rightarrow y + 4 < 0\]
\[f^{-1}(x) = -4 - \sqrt{\dfrac{-(x + 5)}{3}}\]
Why: \(y + 4\) must be negative, so we keep the \(-\) root.

Domain and range of \(f^{-1}\)
\[\text{Domain } f^{-1} = \text{Range } f = (-\infty,\ -5)\]
\[\text{Range } f^{-1} = \text{Domain } f = (-\infty,\ -4)\]
Why: the inputs of \(f^{-1}\) are the outputs of \(f\), and its outputs are the inputs of \(f\). Since \(x < -5\), the root is positive and \(f^{-1}(x)\) is strictly less than \(-4\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (book page 296) prints Range \(f^{-1} = (-\infty,\ -4]\) for Q3 (vi). The domain of \(f\) is \(x < -4\) (strict), so \(-4\) is not an output of \(f^{-1}\): the correct range is \((-\infty,\ -4)\).
